hero.title: Astro reaches for the stars. Mica keeps your content down to earth.

how.title: One model. Forms for editors. Files for your build.
how.lead: The content model connects the editor and the website. Git connects everything else.

steps.title: Describe your content
steps.text: Write the content model in TypeScript, next to your pages. Fields, labels, help texts and rules live in one file.

steps.title: Editors fill in forms
steps.text: Mica turns the model into forms. Editors save as often as they like. Nothing goes on the website until someone publishes.

steps.title: Publish makes one commit
steps.text: Publish commits the saved JSON, Markdoc and images to your repository, as one commit. Your build reads the files. The website never calls Mica.

audiences.title: Calm for editors. Plain for developers.

groups.title: For editors
groups.text: Clear forms with the labels and help that your developer wrote. Rich text, images, relations and lists that you can reorder. No Git words, no YAML.

points.text: Save as often as you like
See each change before you publish
Choose what goes on the website
Keep mine or use theirs when two people edit

groups.title: For developers
groups.text: The model is TypeScript. The content is JSON, Markdoc and images in your repository. Astro reads it at build time, with types.

points.text: No database, no content API, no webhook
One reviewable commit for each publish

agents.title: Your agent edits too. It saves drafts, like everybody else.
agents.lead: Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or any other MCP client can read your content model and change your content. It follows the rules of the editor. A person publishes the drafts.

points.text: Reads the content model, and Mica checks every value
Saves drafts. Publishing by an agent is off, unless you turn it on
Sends the revision it read, so it never overwrites a newer save
Local: npx mica start serves the tools. Self-hosted: you opt in, and each person allows each agent

run.title: On your laptop, or on your server.
run.lead: Both edit the same files in the same repository. Start with one, and add the other when you need it.

options.title: Local editor
options.text: Runs on your machine, next to astro dev. Publish commits and pushes with your own Git credentials.

needs.text: No sign-in, no account, no database

options.title: Self-hosted editor
options.text: One container on your server. Editors sign in through your identity provider, for example Google. Mica keeps its own Git clone.

needs.text: A server with Docker Compose and one volume
A token that can push to the repository

fit.title: Small on purpose.
fit.lead: Mica does a few things well. Here is what it does not do yet, so that you can choose well.

good.text: A content-driven Astro website: a company site, a blog, documentation
One developer, and two to five people who write
Content in Git, as files that people can read
A static website with no CMS code in it

not.text: A preview of drafts in the self-hosted editor
Roles or approval steps inside the editor
A page builder, or editing on the page

start.title: Start in five minutes.
start.text: Give one prompt to your coding agent. It reads the setup guide, asks you about your content, and shows you a plan before it changes anything. Or install Mica by hand.

paths.label: Add Mica to your existing Astro site
paths.content: Read https://micacms.com/setup.md and extend this existing Astro project to work with Mica.

paths.label: Create a new website with Astro and Mica
paths.content: Read https://micacms.com/setup.md and create a new website with Astro and Mica in this folder.

paths.label: Migrate your website from another CMS
Install manually
paths.content:
# 1) Install the Mica packages
npm install @micacms/astro @micacms/core

# 2) Set up your content model; see https://micacms.com/docs/content-model/

# 3) Start the local Mica editor
npx @micacms/editor start
